We run Patchwork CI on 1,200 repositories now, and about 900 of them are open source. When we launched, we promised the tool would always be free for open source, and many people told us that was a bad business decision and asked how we would make money.

Across all those repositories, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. That means developers are spending hours on red builds that aren't real failures.

Open source gave us users, data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.

1,000 families.

14 months ago, Pebble Pantry was a note on my phone, written on maternity leave. Sleep-deprived, staring into an empty fridge at 7pm.

Today, 1,000 families pay €4.99 a month to make dinner time a little easier.

We never ran ads. No growth hacks. Most families found us through school WhatsApp groups, one parent telling another. That's parents trusting us enough to put our name in front of their friends.

So to every mum and dad who shared us in a group chat: you built this with us. Thank you.

And if you're a founder building on a shoestring: keep going. Your community is what carries you.

Why we stopped billing by the hour.

When we started Fernway Studio, we billed hourly, like every agency does. Then 4 of our first 6 projects blew past budget. Clients got frustrated. So did we. Trust started to slip.

So in 2024 we picked a number and stuck to it: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. That's it.

Clients know what they're paying before we start. We work smarter, not longer. And nobody asks for a timesheet anymore.

Since the switch, we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 ran past our 6-week timeline.

Founders, how do you price your work? Tell me in the comments.

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

Our first big customer left Ledgerline 5 months in. That loss changed how we build.

The reason they walked: they had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That work changed how we think about customers. We build for how they actually use their systems now, not just for what's standard.

Today we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

That first customer leaving is why we kept the rest. When customers push back hard, they're telling you what to build. Listen.

We built an app for Rotaship. Nobody used it.

At launch we were proud of it. Sleek, modern, the kind of design you show off. Then the numbers came in: in the first month, only 12% of restaurant staff even opened it.

That stung, but it taught us something. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding to it. Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we moved everything into WhatsApp. All of it.

Now 140 outlets run on it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If you're building for restaurant staff, build where they already are. Don't make them come to you. We had to let go of the app we loved to figure that out.

I spent 11 years in a clinic. Then I walked away.

I still loved being a vet. But one thing kept breaking my heart: anxious pets so terrified we had to sedate them just to examine them. Every day, the same thing.

So in 2023, I founded Doorstep Vet. The idea was simple: bring compassionate, high-quality care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. And every single one reminds me why I left. The pets are calmer. The owners are happier. The medicine is better.

In September, we raised Tabwise's price from $8 to $12 per user per month. A 50% jump, and honestly the scariest decision in the company's history.

Why do it? Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. We could cut quality or charge what we're worth. We charged.

But we didn't leave existing customers behind. Everyone who was already on the product kept their $8 price for 12 months.

The result: 2 out of 140 customers churned in the following 2 months. Two.

Customers pay for outcomes, not software. Price accordingly.

#Hiring #SalesJobs #London #StartupJobs #JoinOurTeam

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. Instead, we recalled and replaced every one of those 400 labels at our own cost, which set us back about $7,000. It hurt, but it kept our customers' trust.

We also introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, there have been zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

To other hardware founders: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

A spindle failure shut down our production line for 3 days.

Years ago, I worked as a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune. One day a spindle failed, and an entire production line was down for 3 days. The warning signs had been there: 2 weeks earlier, vibration readings had clearly shown the problem. No one was watching them.

That experience led me to found Ferrous in 2022, to prevent this kind of avoidable downtime for manufacturers.

Today our sensors are on 410 machines across 17 plants. Every reading tells us something, every alert is a breakdown caught before it happens, and every plant brings Indian manufacturing closer to that goal.

Data only helps if someone is listening.

#Manufacturing #Industry40 #PredictiveMaintenance #MakeInIndia #StartupStory

$50K MRR. Bootstrapped. 18 months.

I started Crateful and people told me I'd need VC money to compete. That a team of three couldn't keep up. That bootstrapping was too slow.

Eighteen months later: $50,000 in monthly recurring revenue, zero outside funding, and the same team of 3.

Here's what did it. The Shopify App Store. About 60% of our signups come from there. We put the app where Shopify merchants were already searching, and they found us.

If you're up late building without funding, keep going. Profitability beats hype. Sustainable growth beats vanity metrics. That's been true for us.

What helped you grow without funding? Tell me below.

For years, Northbound Talent charged the standard recruiting fee: 25% of first-year salary. Our average fee came to about $41,000 per hire.
